frontier_question: Why did OpenAI release o3 and o4-mini in April 2025, and what did the launch signal about the direction of frontier reasoning models?

chunks.content: OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on 2025-04-16 — the first OpenAI reasoning models with vision built into the model itself, not bolted on, and with native tool use (web search, code interpreter) trained into the model. The launch was API-first: o3 and o4-mini were available to developers from day one, and o3 was not in the ChatGPT app at launch (o4-mini was). The technique was budget forcing — a fixed maximum thought budget with task-adaptive (dynamic) compute, so harder questions think longer — and OpenAI's first private chain-of-thought policy (reasoning tokens not exposed to API callers, announced in the o3/o4-mini system card). Pricing: o3 at $10 / $40 per million tokens (input/output), o4-mini at $1.10 / $4.40. o3 set a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark — about 87.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute, at or above the ~85% human baseline, the first model to reach it. With GPT-5 not yet shipping, OpenAI used the launch to defend the reasoning-model frontier against DeepSeek's R1 cost shock and Anthropic's agentic-coding push — reframing frontier capability as tool-using reasoning at commodity prices.

prior_gap_texts: OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 [Source: ev-1].
The launch signaled that the direction of frontier reasoning models was shifting toward "tool-using reasoning at commodity prices" [Source: ev-1].
This strategic move was intended to defend OpenAI’s position against DeepSeek's R1 cost shock and Anthropic's agentic-coding push while GPT-5 had not yet shipped [Source: ev-1].
*   **Native Tool Use:** They featured native tool use, including web search and code interpreter, which was trained into the model [Source: ev-1].

*   **Budget Forcing:** The models utilized a technique called "budget forcing," employing a fixed maximum thought budget with task-adaptive (dynamic) compute so that harder questions required longer thinking times [Source: ev-1].
*   **Private Chain-of-Thought:** This launch introduced OpenAI's first private chain-of-thought policy, where reasoning tokens are not exposed to API callers [Source: ev-1].
The launch also demonstrated significant performance improvements. [Source: ev-1]
o3 set a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark, achieving approximately 87.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute [Source: ev-1].

Pricing for these models was structured as follows:
*   **o3:** $10 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

*   **o4-mini:** $1.10 per million input tokens and $$4.40$ per million output tokens [Note: The evidence lists "1.10 / 4.40" in the context of pricing; interpreting standard token pricing formats implies dollars] [Source: ev-1].
Notably, o3 was not included in the ChatGPT app at launch, whereas o4-mini was [Source: ev-1].
